name: 3D tactics battlefield on a heightmap grid
oneLiner: A small three.js battlefield of terraced tiles (grass, stone, sand, water) with trees, rocks and ruins: select a unit to see its move range (height cost, jump limit, water), a path arrow over the terraces, attack and enemy threat ranges; turn the camera in 90-degree steps and zoom; low-poly units walk tile by tile, hop up terraces, lunge, cast, flinch and fall, always facing where they go or whom they hit.
notFor: devices without WebGL as the main target (a 2D fallback map is shown)

needs: three.js 0.149.0 (window.THREE, three.min.js next to the page)
a WebGL canvas and a 2D overlay canvas stacked on it
map rows: height level per tile, terrain per tile (grass / stone / sand / water), props (tree, pine, rock, ruin)
unit list {id, side, cls, x, z, hp, mv, jump, rng}
a fixed-step update (60 Hz) and a draw pass
provides: rules: reachOf (move points, height cost, jump / fall limits, water and props block, enemies block), pathTo, attackTiles, canHit, threatOf
overlays: move, attack, threat, target tiles, path arrow, cursor
animation: walk tile by tile with hops, melee lunge, cast / arrow projectiles, hurt, defeat, with onStep / onImpact / onDone callbacks
camera: 90-degree turns, zoom, follow, shake; screen-direction to grid-direction mapping
data: anchorOf(id) world->screen box, pickTile(x, y), tileToScreen, state() with facesMove / facesTarget / feetOk

params.label: Extra move cost per level climbed

assets: none: terrain textures, props, units, sky, overlays and UI are drawn by code; three.js 0.149.0 (MIT) is the only dependency (vendor/three@0.149.0/three.min.js, copied next to the page as three.min.js)
